route: Special Work Permit – Artists and Athletes

permit.applies: The petitioning (engaging) company, at the Bureau of Immigration's Main Office, with a sworn certification that the artist will work exclusively for it.
permit.first: An engagement by a petitioning company in the Philippines; the application is filed at least three working days before the event.

fees.what: Late filing (less than three working days before the event), per day per applicant

permit.eligibility: Artists performing in concerts, musicals, or public performances, including but not limited to, members of the production staff and crew

sources.title: Bureau of Immigration Philippines, Special Work Permit – Artists and Athletes
sources.said: The following foreign nationals are required to secure an SWP for a maximum of six (6) months, non-renewable, with an initial duration of not more than three (3) months plus a final three (3) month period, if applicable: Artists performing in concerts, musicals, or public performances, including but not limited to, members of the production staff and crew; … Certification under oath issued by an authorized officer of the petitioning company stating: (i) the SWP request is applicant(s) first or extension; (ii) the artist/athlete will work exclusively for the petitioning company; … Claim the approved SWP 2-3 days after submission. … Miscellaneous Fees: P5,440 Express Lane Fees: P2,000 Total Fees: P7,440 *The SWP application should be submitted at least three (3) working days prior to the scheduled event to avoid incurring late filing fees of two thousand pesos (P2,000) per day per applicant*

blockers.sought: Any union or guild consultation for a foreign performer's SWP

tried.institution: The Bureau of Immigration's SWP page asks only the forms and the company's sworn certification; no union step.
tried.official-register: No rule asking a union consultation for the SWP found.
